## Automated checks

CI ran the 778-test Python suite on Linux and Windows, with explicit skips for tests specific to the other platform (2 on Linux, 86 on Windows). The candidate passed 166 tests of the CI and publication procedures. An additional test of the exact revision of `.gitignore` accompanies the acceptance record. Ruff, documentation links and distribution checks passed.

The scientific checks executed the actual R scripts in the distributed image. They covered all four analyses, automatic workflows, SNP equivalence across uppercase and lowercase panels, preservation of inputs, BAM/pileup comparisons, single- and multi-sample DNP runs, uncovered sites, checks on counts and frequencies, numerical regressions for CPI and Contamination, workflow composition and isolation of failed stages. The R scripts and their integrity manifest were unchanged.

The Windows checks exercised PowerShell, the launcher and the packaged client with its embedded Python. They checked integrity, navigation, plan construction and input mounts. The report `windows-client-check.json` records `wsl_execution: false` and `scientific_execution: false`. The test did not perform a fresh WSL installation on a Windows desktop.

On Ubuntu 24.04 amd64, the checks covered dependency installation in a clean container, DEB installation on a prepared runner, execution as a non-root user, all analyses, the automatic workflow, repeated application launches, reinstallation and removal with data preservation. The upgrade test installed the public 0.7.1 DEB, prepared its runtime, installed the 0.7.2 candidate and ran the self-tests. Results, preferences, user data and the shared Docker configuration were preserved. These runner tests cover the prepared configuration. Manual qualification across desktop configurations remains outside their scope.

`qualification-evidence.zip` includes only logs, reports and synthetic data from the automated checks. Its descriptor verifies each entry's identity, size and SHA-256. The release retains the reports, inventory and archive beyond the retention period of the temporary Actions artifacts.

## Historical manual evidence and source comparison

The [earlier manual observation](https://github.com/GregorioDalia/nipat-desktop/blob/1603d998e036ba73d37f015338c1200c1ea12c65/.github/release-acceptance/v0.7.1-evidence.md) applies to commit `1b601081a4aff9efe1806c921fd7ac963feea7b7`. It records a ready Windows installation and a successful DNPcall → Contamination workflow on a real BAM, with 11 DNP sites and 10 informative sites for Contamination. This is historical platform evidence. The 0.7.2 candidate did not undergo that manual test.

The acceptance record identifies 81 changed operational files with SHA-256 hashes before and after the changes, and 139 unchanged operational files. Changes cover Python validation, orchestration, the client, installers, runtime and tests. The protected R sources were unchanged. The record makes no claim of operational equivalence with the historical version.

## Scope and limitations

The decision covers a pre-1.0 release for research and domain validation. The record explicitly defers the six complete desktop acceptance scenarios, including scenarios with partial automated coverage. Validation using the researchers' data and interpretations remains pending.

Version 0.7.2 provides diagnostics for incomplete runs, selective shutdown of identified containers, runtime maintenance and repair of the current installation. The release does not claim complete transactional rollback to a previous version or a fully translated interface. Periodic dependency monitoring produces reports. These reports do not certify security or sign the software.
